subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the levels of organisation, smallest to largest?
questions.explain: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs make organ systems.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotic cells have genetic material not enclosed in a nucleus
Eukaryotic cells have no membrane-bound nucleus
Prokaryotic cells are larger than eukaryotic cells
questions.explain: Prokaryotes lack a true nucleus, whereas eukaryotes (plants, animals) have membrane-bound organelles including a nucleus.

questions.q: What is the function of ribosomes?
questions.explain: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

questions.q: What is the main function of the nucleus in a eukaryotic cell?
options: Controlling what enters and leaves the cell
Controlling the cell and storing genetic material
questions.explain: The nucleus contains the DNA and controls the cell's activities.

questions.q: A cell is 0.05 mm wide. What is this in micrometres (µm)?
What is the function of the cell wall in a plant cell?
options: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explain: The plant cell wall is made of cellulose and provides strength and support.

questions.q: A root hair cell has a long projection. How does this help its function?
options: It allows the cell to photosynthesise
It increases surface area for absorbing water and minerals
It helps the cell carry oxygen
questions.explain: The long extension gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions.

questions.q: Which feature is present in a bacterial (prokaryotic) cell?
options: A single loop of DNA in the cytoplasm
questions.explain: Bacteria have no nucleus; their genetic material is a single circular DNA loop free in the cytoplasm, sometimes with plasmids.

questions.q: A sperm cell has many mitochondria. What is this an adaptation for?
options: Providing energy for the tail to swim to the egg
questions.explain: The many mitochondria release energy for the flagellum (tail) to swim to the egg.

questions.q: An image of a cell is 30 mm long and the magnification is ×1500. What is the actual size?
questions.explain: Actual = image ÷ magnification = 30 mm ÷ 1500 = 0.02 mm = 20 µm.

questions.q: Which structure is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
questions.explain: Chloroplasts (along with cell wall and permanent vacuole) are plant-specific, while the others are common to both.
